one_month_reasoning: The main in-window event is Q3 2026 results. The date is not yet announced (the latest SEC filings are the Sep 8 PTFI revolver 8-K and the Sep 24 Form SD), but FCX has reported Q3 on Oct 19-23 every year and reports on Thursdays, so ~Thu Oct 22 is most likely. Consensus Q3 EPS is $0.74 (corrected from the $0.77 I cited in round 1). Guidance is 750M lb Q3 copper sales at $2.00/lb unit cost with a $6.00 H2 deck, while copper traded mostly above that in the quarter. That points to a modest price-driven beat, but FCX fell on its Q2 beat, so I take no strong earnings view. The Section 232 refined-copper tariff is still undecided after the notional window lapsed on Sep 28. Because the front-month COMEX premium is already ~zero (SMM, Sep 29), a 'no tariff' headline would do less near-term damage than I assumed in round 1, so I remove most of my small downside drag. Net: roughly symmetric lognormal around $70.58 at ~13.7% monthly vol (48%/3.5), with P(>=spot) at 0.49.

fair_value.method: Blend of attributable P/E on 2027E EPS ~$3.98 (a $6.15 deck gives ~$17.0B EBITDA; 32% tax, 40% NCI, 1.444B shares) x 17x = $68, an FCF-yield value of $70 (62% attributable), a mid-cycle P/E of $62 at $5.25 copper and a 2028 full-Grasberg P/E of $70. Weighted 45/30/15/10 this gives ~$68, a little below the $70.58 spot and ~4% below the $4.16 consensus EPS.

I still assume partial mean reversion, toward Goldman-type ~$5.2-5.5 fair values, and the risk that ~770k st of COMEX stocks returns to the market. That puts the deck at $6.15, up from $6.00 in round 1.
Linear interpolation of management's range: $13B + 1.15 x $3.5B per $1/lb. In round 1 I used the $390M/$0.10 point sensitivity, which is steeper than the $13-20B endpoints imply.
The 2026 guided ETR is ~30% (Peru 40%, Indonesia 36%, US 7%; Q2 release footnote d). A higher Indonesian mix in 2027 moves it to ~32%.

At $70.58 the stock trades at ~17x consensus 2027 EPS of $4.16 (17 analysts, range $2.62-5.69). Volume growth into 2028 supports a mid-to-high-teens multiple, trimmed because these are near-peak-price earnings.

bear.story: LME retreats toward ~$4.75-5.00/lb: demand slows and, if the tariff is dropped, ~770k st of COMEX stocks returns to the global market (the front-month COMEX premium is already gone, so the downside runs through LME, not a COMEX-LME convergence). A Grasberg ramp setback (PB2/3 capped at ~60% until the ore-loading fix) or adverse IUPK terms add to it. 2027 EPS ~$2.8 at 16x.

base.story: Grasberg reaches ~80% by mid-2027 and 2027 copper sales rise >20% (>=3.72B lb) with gold up >50%. Copper averages ~$5.9-6.4 and the IUPK extension is granted. EPS ~$4.0 in 2027 and ~$4.4 in 2028, and the market pays ~16-17x.

bull.story: Mine disruptions keep supply short and copper holds above $7/lb (EBITDA >$20B). The leach push toward 800Mlb is validated and Bagdad goes ahead. EPS ~$5.5 x 18x.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$46 (~35% down) the stock would be discounting LME copper sustainably under ~$5/lb (~$13B EBITDA, ~$2.9-3.0 EPS) or a failure of the Grasberg recovery or the IUPK extension (economic interest already steps down to ~37% from 2042). That would break the volume-plus-price thesis fundamentally; it is not ordinary 48%-vol noise.

reasoning: Round 2 changes are small and the view is unchanged: no valuation edge at spot. The supervisor confirmed consensus 2027 EPS at $4.16 (17 analysts), in line with my bridge, and corrected Q3 consensus to $0.74. It showed that the front-month COMEX tariff premium has collapsed (Oct-26 COMEX $47/t below LME 3M on Sep 29), so I stop treating spot as a tariff artifact and restate the tariff risk as LME tightness from US stock hoarding that could reverse. That lifts my 2027 deck from $6.00 to $6.15. Re-reading the Q2 release, NCI took 52% of H1 2025 net income at full Grasberg, so I raise my 2027 NCI share to 40% and cut the FCF attributable share to 62%, as the supervisor suggested. I also correct my EBITDA interpolation to the $13-20B endpoints ($3.5B per $1/lb). The net effect is 2027 EPS of ~$3.98 (vs $4.10), P/E $68, FCF $70, mid-cycle $62, plus a new 2028 full-Grasberg leg at $70, for a blended fair value of ~$68 (vs $69). This is slightly below spot and consensus; I stay a touch more conservative than consensus on NCI leakage. I agree with the supervisor's $5.3B net debt, but my methods are attributable P/E and FCF, so it does not enter directly. Distribution: median ~$70, lognormal sigma ~0.42 with a slightly fat left tail. The upper body is trimmed by ~0.005 to reflect the lower fair value; the lower tail is unchanged. Scenarios $45/$71/$100 at 25/50/25 give a mean of ~$72. For the 1-month ladder I removed most of the downside drag because the tariff-premium unwind has already happened at the front of the curve. Extra research was limited to SEC EDGAR (the filing index and the Q2 release).
